calls.head: The Sharks will send Nurse and Kesselring at Pastrňák
calls.body: At home, the Sharks keep sending Nurse and Kesselring out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Warsofsky has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Bruins’ first line is Pastrňák, Zacha and Geekie.

calls.body: On shots from defensemen, San Jose is one of the league’s best, but Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Sharks’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Bruins beat the Sharks
paras: Charlie McAvoy played his first game of the season, after missing the first six. Fraser Minten opened the scoring for the Bruins midway through the first. Jacob Trouba scored his first goal for San Jose 2:34 later to tie it 1-1. McAvoy gave the Bruins the lead 3:14 later. Ivar Stenberg, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Macklin Celebrini, on the power play early in the second to tie it 2-2. Matthew Poitras gave the Bruins the lead 2:54 later. Pavel Zacha made it 4-2 late in the second. Celebrini pulled the Sharks within one on the power play early in the third. Minten scored his second of the night midway through the third to make it 5-3 for the Bruins. Will Borgen scored his first goal for Boston with 1:42 left into the empty net with 1:42 left.
The chances were closer than the score. Jeremy Swayman made 35 saves for the Bruins, and Yaroslav Askarov allowed five goals on 25 shots.
Darnell Nurse and Nikita Zadorov fought midway through the third. The Bruins moved to 5-2-0, and the Sharks dropped to 3-3-0.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Bruins.
Mason Marchment’s five-game point streak against Boston ended.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
